subject.title: Embedded agent: auto-rotate (or persist a marker) on context-overflow give_up instead of wedging the session until manual /reset

question: Should OpenClaw accept marker-first persistent blocked-overflow recovery for exhausted embedded-agent context overflow, or require guarded one-shot rotation and replay before adding a durable marker contract?
rationale: Current source and docs intentionally preserve the session mapping with manual recovery, while the issue and linked PR introduce a durable core session-state contract and leave broader replay/rotation semantics to product judgment.

options.title: Accept marker-first recovery
options.body: Proceed with a durable overflow-blocked marker after compatibility review, leaving automatic rotation and replay safety for separate design work.

options.title: Require guarded rotation first
options.body: Use the issue to design one-shot rotation with replay-safety gates and loop caps before accepting a marker-only recovery path.

options.title: Keep manual recovery with diagnostics
options.body: Keep the documented manual `/reset` or `/new` behavior and limit changes to visibility, docs, or operator diagnostics.

recommendation.title: Accept marker-first recovery
recommendation.body: Proceed with a durable overflow-blocked marker after compatibility review, leaving automatic rotation and replay safety for separate design work.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is primarily about durable session state, recovery semantics, and product boundaries, where the recent history and prior review context point most strongly to this account.
